title: How did the electric telegraph send words down a wire?
aliases: dots and dashes in a telegraph
answer: People used an electric telegraph to send messages between places joined by a wire. At one end, an operator pressed a key to turn the signal on and off. At the other end, a machine made marks or sounds at matching times. Short and long signals could stand for letters in a system called Morse code. An operator who knew the code could turn those marks or sounds back into words.
facts: An early U.S. telegraph line carried a message from Washington to Baltimore in 1844.

title: How did a wire let messages cross the ocean?
answer: A telegraph cable stretched across the Atlantic could carry pulses from one shore to the other. A ship laid the cable along the ocean floor between Ireland and Newfoundland. A covering helped keep seawater away from the wires inside. Before that link, news had to travel across the ocean with a ship. A message on a working cable could arrive while the sender was still near the telegraph key.
facts: A lasting transatlantic telegraph cable began working in 1866 after earlier attempts.

title: How could an early telephone carry a voice down a wire?
answer: When someone speaks, waves in the air make thin parts of a telephone shake. In an early wired telephone, a moving part changed an electrical signal that traveled down a wire. At the other end, the changing signal made a different thin part shake. Its motion pushed the nearby air and a listener could hear something like the original voice. Unlike in a telegraph, each person could speak right away without knowing a code.
facts: Alexander Graham Bell patented an early telephone in 1876.

title: How did a switchboard connect two people on the telephone?
aliases: how phone calls connected before dial
answer: At an early telephone exchange, lines from many homes and businesses reached one switchboard. When one person wanted to call another, an operator found both lines. The operator plugged in cords to join the two lines for that call. Once it was over, the cords could be used to connect different people. Later equipment handled many of these steps automatically, so callers could dial a number without asking for an operator first.
facts: A switchboard could connect different pairs of calls at the same time.

title: How could a typewriter make one printed letter at a time?
answer: In a common mechanical typewriter, each key moves a piece of metal with a raised letter or number at its end. When it hits an inked ribbon, the ribbon leaves that character on the paper. The machine moves the paper holder a little to make room for the next letter. When the writer reaches the end of a line, moving the holder back brings a fresh line into place.
facts: An early successful typewriter already used the QWERTY order still found on many computer keyboards.

title: How can six keys make a raised braille character?
aliases: how braille is printed with keys
answer: A basic braille cell has room for six raised dots in two columns. A braille writer has one dot key for each position. To make a character, the writer presses the needed keys together. The machine presses raised bumps into thick paper at those spots. After feeling the dots, a reader can recognize the pattern. Holding two keys at the same time makes a single character containing two raised dots in the right places.
facts: A computer can also take braille input from six keys set up for that purpose.

title: How can a little hole make an image inside a dark room?
aliases: why pinhole pictures are upside down
answer: If a room is dark and there is a small hole in one wall, light from outdoors can enter and make an image on the wall across from the hole. Light travels in nearly straight lines through the air. Rays from high parts of the scene go downward after passing through the hole. Rays from low parts go upward. The scene appears upside down on the wall, even though everything outside stayed right side up.
facts: People call this setup a camera obscura, which means dark room.

title: What made a daguerreotype different from a modern print?
answer: A daguerreotype is an early type of photograph. The image sits on a thin coat of silver over a copper plate. Tilt the plate in the light and some parts can look lighter or darker as the shiny surface reflects what is around it. Each plate held a single original image. If someone wanted another picture, the plate could not simply be used to print a stack of matching copies on paper.
facts: The process was announced in France in 1839.

title: How did a roll of film change what a camera could do?
aliases: first Kodak camera send back to process
answer: A roll of photographic film can hold several pictures along the same strip. Light enters the camera and leaves an image on one part of the film. Turning a handle moves that part away so a clean stretch is ready for another picture. In 1888, the first Kodak camera came with film already loaded. Its owner could take pictures and send the camera away to have the pictures made visible and printed.
facts: The original Kodak could take up to 100 pictures on a roll.

title: Why does a movie look like it moves when it is made of still pictures?
answer: A movie shows a row of still pictures called frames one after another. In each frame, people and objects may be in a slightly different place. If the changes come in the right order and quickly enough, our eyes and brain can follow them as movement. A ball can look as if it rolls across a screen, even though every picture shows the ball stopped in one place.
facts: Playing the same pictures faster can make the motion look faster.

title: How could gears add numbers inside a machine?
answer: In the 1800s Charles Babbage designed a machine to calculate long lists of numbers. A wheel in the machine could stand for a digit. When a wheel passed from nine back to zero, it could make the wheel beside it move one place. That worked like carrying a one in written addition. Repeating simple changes let his machine fill a table with results. Turning the mechanism supplied the motion.
facts: The Difference Engine was designed to use mechanical parts to calculate, rather than electric circuits.

title: What did Ada Lovelace imagine a calculating machine could do?
answer: Ada Lovelace wrote about a design for a machine called the Analytical Engine. She explained a way to give it steps for calculating a series of numbers. She also thought about what a machine might do if its numbers stood for things besides amounts, such as parts of music. The whole machine was never finished in her lifetime. Her notes showed that the way instructions are arranged matters as much as the machine that follows them.
facts: Lovelace’s notes about Charles Babbage’s design appeared in 1843.

title: How could holes in paper help count people?
answer: Before modern computers, clerks could put information about a person on a stiff paper card by making holes in chosen spots. A counting machine checked those spots. If a hole was there, part of the machine could make an electrical connection and add to a count. Sorting the cards made it easier to compare groups. For the 1890 United States census, the same kinds of counting steps could be run over many cards.
facts: Herman Hollerith helped develop the counting and sorting system used for that census.

title: Why was ENIAC so much bigger than a modern computer?
aliases: ENIAC vacuum tubes what was it
answer: ENIAC was an early electronic computer. Its thousands of vacuum tubes helped it switch electrical signals and make calculations quickly. Each tube took up space, and the machine needed many wires and panels to connect them. People set up many early jobs by changing switches and making cable connections. A modern chip puts far more tiny electronic parts in much less space, so a powerful computer can fit in your pocket.
facts: ENIAC filled a large room at the University of Pennsylvania.

title: How can a transistor work like a very small switch?
answer: A transistor is a small electronic part. A signal at one point can control how much electrical current flows through another path. A computer can use this behavior to switch between states that stand for zero and one. The part does not need a moving handle like a room’s light switch. Other circuits can use transistors to help a weak signal control a stronger one, which can be useful in equipment that plays sound.
facts: An early working transistor was built at Bell Labs in 1947.

title: How do many electronic parts fit on a single chip?
answer: An integrated circuit puts many tiny electronic parts on one piece of material. The parts can include transistors and very small tracks that join them. Making the connections as part of the chip saves space. It also lets factories make many copies of the same design. One chip can do a simple job like adding numbers or a larger job like helping a computer follow the instructions for an entire program.
facts: Some of the earliest integrated circuit designs appeared in the late 1950s.

title: Why was an old floppy disk called floppy?
aliases: why is a floppy disk called floppy
answer: An early floppy disk held a thin, flexible circle inside a sleeve. A drive spun the disk and moved a small part over its surface to read or write patterns of magnetism. People could take the disk out and move the information to another computer. Some later floppy disks had hard outer cases, but the disk hidden inside was still flexible. A floppy disk could carry only a small amount compared with many drives today.
facts: IBM used a floppy disk to load computer data in 1971.
